title: The Cat and the Crow
logline: When a leopard corners a cat under their meeting tree, his friend the crow lures a pack of sheepdogs across the meadow to chase the leopard away.
moral: A true friend does not leave you alone in danger; wit can do what strength cannot.
tone: Warm friendship comedy with one stretch of real suspense: quiet and cosy at the start, tight and still while the leopard stalks, fast and funny in the dog chase, tender at the end.

beats.summary: Cat and crow are friends: the head bump that will return at the end.
Their daily meeting place, the big tree at the forest edge.
The routine: crow forages, cat naps in the shade, then they talk.
Eyes in the dark: a leopard appears among the trees.
The slow stalk toward the sleeping cat.
The crow sees the danger and flies to a high branch; the cat is left on the ground.
The trap as a diagram: the leopard is nearer the trunk than the cat.
The cat looks up and calls his friend for help.
The crow thinks fast and spots shepherds, sheep and strong dogs far away.
It lands under the dogs noses and flaps its wings at them.
The dogs snap and miss; the hop and return game begins.
Hop by hop the dogs leave their post and follow.
The chase home: flying low so the dogs keep it in sight, cross-cut with the cat in the bush.
Under the tree the dogs see the leopard beside the cat: the plan is revealed.
The dogs forget the crow and charge the leopard, barking.
The hunter becomes the hunted: the leopard bolts and vanishes.
The cat thanks the crow for not leaving him alone: the head bump again.
Everyone back in place: friends under the tree, dogs with the shepherds, leopard far away.

sets.description: The main set, world 1600 x 1230, ground y 900, composed from Library pieces and baked once. Sky: skyCycle (u 0.25 by day, 0.42 at the end). hillTrees on the horizon. FOREST: treeRow over x 0..480 with a navy halftone darkness rectangle behind the trunks (y 380..900), plus two separate foreground trunks at x 330 and x 470 (60 wide, drawn after the characters as occluders). BIG TREE: tree(ctx, 760, 900, {w: 120, top: 260, crowns: [[760,210,190],[600,290,150],[930,280,160],[1080,340,130],[480,340,110]]}); one bare HIGH BRANCH from the trunk at (800, 410) out to (990, 388), 22 thick, perch point (950, 392). SHADE: blue halftone ellipse centred (1000, 905), 520 x 40. Rest spots: cat (1080, 900), crow (1190, 900). BUSH: Library bush at x 1300, w 240, h 150, drawn after the cat so the cat can hide inside it. Open meadow from x 1420 to 1600 (the dogs enter here). Coordinates are design values; measure the crowns on the baked set.

World 1600 x 1230, ground y 900. sky day, sun, one cloudFlat, hillTrees, ground. Paler meadow green band y 880..900 with grass tufts every 90 units. A 30 % scale silhouette of the big tree on the horizon at x 110 (shows the way home). Guard post x 520..780 (three flattened grass ovals appear when the dogs leave). Flock zone x 950..1400 in two rows (front y 900, back y 884 at 0.88 scale). Shepherd marks at (1120, 884) and (1480, 900).

Planned asset chaseRoad (KD-005), used as a looping strip: every layer is a function of distance travelled D(t), moving right to left on screen. Three parallax layers: far hillTrees (0.15 D), mid grass tufts and small bushes (0.6 D), near ground with landmarks (1.0 D): a stump, a sapling, a rock, a tall grass tuft, at fixed distances. The home tree rides the horizon on the left and scales 12 % to 60 % with D. Ground y 900.

subtitles.ar: كان قط وغراب صديقين،|يلتقيان كل يوم تحت شجرة كبيرة عند طرف الغابة.|كان الغراب يطير بحثًا عن الطعام،|بينما يستريح القط في الظل، ثم يجلسان معًا ويتحدثان.
subtitles.en: A cat and a crow were friends|who met each day beneath a large tree at the forest’s edge.|The crow flew off to find food|while the cat rested in the shade, and later they talked together.

subtitles.ar: وفي يوم كانا تحت الشجرة،|فظهر نمر مفترس بين الأشجار.|رآهما واقترب ببطء، وهو ينظر إلى القط.|انتبه الغراب إلى الخطر، فطار سريعًا إلى غصن مرتفع.
subtitles.en: One day, while they were beneath the tree,|a fierce leopard appeared among the trees.|It approached slowly, watching the cat.|The crow saw the danger and flew to a high branch.

subtitles.ar: أما القط فلم يجد طريقًا آمنًا للهرب.|كان النمر أقرب إليه من جذع الشجرة،|ولم يستطع أن يصعد قبل وصوله.|رفع رأسه ونادى صديقه الغراب طالبًا المساعدة.
subtitles.en: The cat could find no safe escape.|The leopard was nearer the tree trunk,|and the cat could not climb before it arrived.|It looked up and called to its friend the crow for help.

subtitles.ar: فكر الغراب بسرعة.|رأى من بعيد رعاة يقودون أغنامًا،|ومعهم كلاب قوية تحرس القطيع.|طار نحوهم، ثم نزل قريبًا من الكلاب وأخذ يحرك جناحيه أمامها.
subtitles.en: The crow thought quickly.|In the distance it saw shepherds with sheep|and strong dogs guarding the flock.|It flew toward them, swooped close to the dogs, and flapped its wings before them.

subtitles.ar: حاولت الكلاب الإمساك بالغراب،|لكنه كان يبتعد مسافة قصيرة ثم يعود.|وكلما اقتربت منه، طار أمامها مرة أخرى.|وبهذه الطريقة جعل الكلاب تترك مكانها وتتبع طريقه.
subtitles.en: The dogs tried to catch the crow,|but it flew a short distance away and returned.|Each time they approached, it flew ahead again.|In this way it drew the dogs away and made them follow.

subtitles.ar: اتجه الغراب نحو الشجرة التي ينتظر عندها القط.|بقي يطير على ارتفاع منخفض حتى لا تفقده الكلاب من نظرها.|وكانت الكلاب تجري خلفه بسرعة،|دون أن تعرف ما يريد منها.
subtitles.en: The crow headed toward the tree where the cat waited.|It kept flying low so the dogs would not lose sight of it.|They ran after it,|unaware of its plan.

subtitles.ar: عندما وصلت الكلاب إلى الشجرة،|رأت النمر واقفًا قرب القط.|نسيت الغراب في الحال، واندفعت نحو النمر وهي تنبح بقوة.|خاف النمر من الكلاب الكثيرة، فهرب بين الأشجار واختفى.
subtitles.en: When the dogs reached the tree,|they saw the leopard beside the cat.|They instantly forgot the crow and rushed at the leopard, barking fiercely.|Frightened by the pack, the leopard fled into the trees and vanished.

subtitles.ar: خرج القط من مكانه بعدما زال الخطر.|نظر إلى الغراب وشكره لأنه لم يتركه وحده.|عاد الصديقان إلى الشجرة،|بينما رجعت الكلاب إلى الرعاة، وبقي النمر بعيدًا عنهما.
subtitles.en: Once the danger had passed, the cat emerged|and thanked the crow for not abandoning him.|The friends returned to the tree,|while the dogs went back to the shepherds and the leopard stayed away.

new_assets.name: cat
new_assets.description: The planned cat (AN-014) with a second palette (pal 1 white and orange) and the acting fields this film needs: lie 0..1 (curled rest), puff 0..1 (fur and tail bristle), crouch 0..1, ears -1..1, headRot, raise (front paw), talk, mouth (closed, smile, open), brow, eyes wide.
new_assets.implementation: Side view built like the Library fox: body ellipse 130 x 70 with its top 105 above the feet, four legs 50 long driven by ph/amp (same gait code as fox), round head r 42 with two triangle ears (rotation from ears), tail as a tapered 5 point bezier whose control points come from tailUp and tailCurl. arch raises the mid spine control point by 40. puff draws a zigzag outline (seeded, 14 spikes) 8 units outside the body and triples the tail width. lie blends leg length to 0, drops the body to the ground and wraps the tail round the front. Eyes through eye2 so gaze, lid and wet work. pal table CATPAL[0] black (AN-014), [1] white/orange.

new_assets.name: leopard
new_assets.description: Big spotted cat, about 400 x 220 at s 1, reusable as tiger or panther by palette (pal 0 leopard rosettes, later pal 1 tiger stripes, pal 2 black). Fields: ph, amp, crouch 0..1 (stalk), raise (front paw), headTurn 0..1 (looks back over the shoulder), mouth (closed, snarl, open), lick, brow, ears -1..1, tailUp, tailTuck 0..1, eyes wide, plus shared acting fields.
new_assets.implementation: Start from the lion body and leg code without the mane: body rounded box 250 x 105 with its top 185 above the feet, slimmer than the lion; head ellipse 96 x 84 on a short neck, cream muzzle, round ears r 16. Rosettes: seeded list of about 18 points inside the body shape, each a black ring (lineWidth 5, r 11) with a brown dot, clipped to the body. crouch lowers the body 45 and bends the legs so the shoulders sit above the back line. snarl: upper lip polygon lifts to show two white fangs. headTurn mirrors the head group about the neck. tailTuck curves the tail bezier down between the hind legs. Legs from walk().

new_assets.name: dog
new_assets.description: Sheepdog, about 240 x 190 at s 1, three palettes (tan, white with black patches, brown). Fields: ph, amp (trot and gallop), sit 0..1, crouch 0..1 (play bow: chest down, rump up), bark 0..1 (jaw open with a forward jolt), mouth (closed, open, growl), tongue 0..1, ears -1..1, earStream 0..1 (ears blown back when running), tailWag, hackles 0..1, headTilt, brow, plus shared acting fields.
new_assets.implementation: Side view on the fox gait code: body rounded box 150 x 80 with its top 130 above the feet and a deeper chest ellipse at the front, legs 62 long and 20 wide, head box 76 x 62 with a square muzzle 44 x 34, drop ear as a rounded triangle rotated by ears, bushy tail as a fat tapered shape rotated by tailUp + 0.5 * sin(tailWag phase). hackles: 7 small triangles along the back line scaled by the field. bark: lower jaw wedge opens to 0.5 rad and the whole dog shifts 6 units forward for 2 frames. Gallop: amp above 1.3 switches the legs to gathered and stretched pairs with a small spine sq oscillation.

new_assets.name: sheep
new_assets.description: Background sheep, about 190 x 150 at s 1, two wool palettes. Fields: ph, amp, headDown 0..1 (graze), chew, hop.
new_assets.implementation: Wool body as a closed bumpy shape (12 seeded bumps round an ellipse 150 x 95) in white with blue dotPat shading, four black legs 45 long from walk(), black head ellipse 46 x 56 rotating about the neck by headDown, two small ears, eye2 eyes. chew moves the jaw 3 units sideways on a sine.

new_assets.name: forestEdge
new_assets.description: Forest wall on the left, one big tree with a high bare branch, a shade patch, a bush and open meadow on the right; 1600 wide. Reusable for any story set at the edge of a wood.
new_assets.implementation: bake() once from Library skyCycle or sky, hillTrees, treeRow, tree() with the crowns listed under sets, ground, halftoneShadow for the shade. The two foreground trunks and the bush are drawn each frame after the characters (occluders). The high branch is a seg() 22 thick whose tip y takes a swing() offset when the crow lands.

new_assets.name: pasture
new_assets.description: Open grazing meadow, 1600 wide, with a far tree silhouette for orientation. Reusable for any shepherd or flock story.
new_assets.implementation: bake() from sky, sun, cloudFlat, hillTrees, ground plus a paler grass band and seeded tufts; the far tree is the forestEdge tree call at scale 0.3 filled as one dark green silhouette.

new_assets.name: chaseRoad
new_assets.description: The planned tracking chase strip (KD-005), used here in loop mode with meadow landmarks and the home tree growing on the horizon.
new_assets.implementation: Three layers drawn with x = (x0 - k * D(t)) mod L, k 0.15, 0.6, 1.0; D(t) from kfn keys so speed changes (the crow easing off at 108.8) come from one function that also drives every walk() phase.

new_assets.name: inset circle
new_assets.description: The planned round picture in picture with an iris open and close: the crow watching (64.0 to 71.2), the cat in the bush (104.6 to 107.1), the shepherd and dog (160.0 to 161.4).
new_assets.implementation: In panel space: clip to a circle (r 95 to 120), draw the second scene through its own camera, restore, then a fat black brush ring and a thin yellow ring. Iris = radius eased 0 to r over 0.25 s.

new_assets.name: runInPlace
new_assets.description: The planned comic wind up: legs cycle at full run amplitude with no travel for about 0.35 s, dust building behind, then release. Used for the leopard at 140.0.
new_assets.implementation: Feed walk() a virtual distance that keeps increasing while the real x key holds, then switch to the real LX keys; dustBurst behind the hind paws every 3 frames.

owner_questions: The cat is drawn white with orange patches (a new palette of the planned cat) instead of black, so that it stands apart from the black crow and the yellow leopard; default used: white and orange.

A bush is added as the cat hiding place so that "the cat came out of its place" in paragraph 8 can be shown; the leopard only looms over the bush and never touches the cat; default used: bush, no contact.
Numbers not given by the script were chosen as three dogs, five sheep and two shepherds; default used: 3, 5 and 2.
Comic additions beyond the script: the dogs bump heads (82.6), a three dog pile up under the tree (125.3) and a shepherd shouting HEY! (98.2); default used: all three kept.
Invented English lettering: CAW!, MEOW!, HELP!, FLAP! FLAP!, SNAP!, WOOF! WOOF! WOOF!, POP!, ZIP!, HEY!, LUNCH?, the labels and counters, and the time card ONE DAY...; default used: as listed.
For "the leopard stayed away" the ending shows only its eyes far inside the forest, which go out when the crow caws; default used: eyes only, no second appearance of the animal.
The crow plan is not explained in advance (no thought cloud showing dogs chasing the leopard) so that the reveal at 126.84 is a surprise; default used: plan kept secret.
implementation_notes: Screen direction: home (tree, forest) is always LEFT and the pasture RIGHT. The crow flies out left to right; the lure and the chase always run right to left; in forestEdge the dogs enter from the right edge and the leopard flees left into the forest.

Leopard position over time in forestEdge (ground y 900): 380 at 26.8; 560 at 33.6; 640 at 46.4; 700 at 53; 900 at 59.5; 1130 from 105 to 133; backs to 960 by 139.9; 380 at 141.3; hidden after 142.5. Drive every move with one LX kfn and walk(LX, t) so paws never slide.
Cat position: 1080 (rest spot) to 53.5; backs to 1290 by 54.8; inside the bush (1310) from about 59 to 144.7; out to 1180 by 146.5; back to 1080 by 156.5.
Draw order in forestEdge: baked set, shade, leopard, cat, bush, dogs, crow, foreground trunks, lettering. When the cat is inside the bush draw only peekEyes over the bush at (1310, 850).
Set LIFE.t = t each frame for automatic blinks; use noBlink during the freezes at 34.3, 62.7 and 126.8 to 127.4.

Groups never move in unison: use stagger(i) of 3 to 4 frames for the three dogs and seeded phases for the five sheep. Keep the three dog personalities (dog1 bold, dog2 copycat, dog3 slow and puzzled) in every shot.
Use twoShot() for S6 (cat and crow heads) and S15; keep both faces inside the panel with a margin of 120.
Panel-only shake (3 units or less) on the barks at 135.4 and the gallop in S12; the caption panel never moves.
Diagram elements in S5 (dotted paths, X marks, distance bars) are drawn in world space under the ground line or above heads, never across a face; remove each within 2 s.

S7 opens on the forestEdge set (crow close-up) and whips to the pasture at 64.0; hide the set change inside the 5 frame whip. The inset in S7 and S8 draws the crow on the forestEdge branch through a second camera.

Sound effects only at: 3.4 pop, 13.6 pop, 20.3 whoosh (card), 24.4 rustle, 28.6 thud, 40.6 thud, 46.1 thud, 122.3 whoosh, 144.3 chime, 147.8 pop, 149.4 pop, 164.5 chime. Barks, snaps and caws are lettering only, with no sound, because the narration runs over them.
The ONE DAY... card covers 19.9 to 20.9 (the pause); change the sky and reset poses at its covered midpoint 20.4.
Call the style finish primitive last in every frame. Lettering: headlines 44 px or more, labels 28 px or more at 1280 x 720 scale; no en or em dashes.
warnings: Four new animals (cat, leopard, dog, sheep) is the upper limit for one film; cat is already planned for AN-014 and should be drawn once for both. If time is short, sheep can be simplified to static wool shapes with a head bob.
